column1: # Sample sheet - Project 23, ancient DNA authentication
# Verified against ENA 2026-10-06. Tab-separated. One row per sample;
# `runs` is a semicolon-separated list of runs merged into that sample.
# The design is a CONTRAST. Task 7 asks us to distinguish genuinely ancient
# molecules from modern contamination, and a pipeline that reports "damage
# found" on one ancient sample has demonstrated nothing. Each sample below has
# a different EXPECTED damage signal, so the estimator is tested against cases
# where it must fire and cases where it must stay silent:
#   undeclared  -> ancient, protocol NOT stated in ENA   -> no expectation; the data tell us
#   partial_udg -> ancient, interior uracils excised -> expect spike confined to terminal base
#   full_udg    -> ancient, all uracils excised      -> expect FLAT (biological negative)
#   modern      -> never ancient                     -> expect FLAT (true negative)
# Protocol labels come from ENA's library_construction_protocol field. Only the
# two plague capture studies declare one; for the rest it is empty, so we do not
# assume a protocol and instead report what the damage profile itself implies.
# If the estimator fires on `modern`, the estimator is broken. If it fires on
# `full_udg`, we have confused a lab protocol for antiquity. The partial_udg
# case is the sharpest test, because its damage is real but confined to one base.
